- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.6), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 1–2% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates near-term peak; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak observed in 7–10 day window.
- Model underestimates true mean reversion when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to align with historical mean of last 18 days.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–), model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead by 0.5–1.0% to capture momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price by 0.5–2.5% in early period (days 1–10); apply +0.75% bias to first 5 days of forecast.
